stemBlocks.value: Make x the subject of the formula y = x + 9.
Think first: You are rearranging, not solving for a number, so the answer will be an expression in y.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p055-q01 from workbook page 55.

solutionSteps.instruction: Identify what is being done to x.

contentBlocks.value: an equation may be read in either direction

strategyBlocks.value: Undo the addition of 9 by subtracting 9 from both sides.

whyThisWorks.value: Changing the subject uses exactly the same balancing rules as solving an equation; the only difference is that the answer is an expression rather than a number. Subtracting 9 from both sides undoes the addition and leaves x alone on one side. Because equality is symmetric, y − 9 = x and x = y − 9 say the same thing.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing x = y + 9 by repeating the operation instead of reversing it.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing x = y + 9 by repeating the operation instead of reversing it.

commonErrors.misconception: Stopping at y − 9 = x when the question asks for x as the subject.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Stopping at y − 9 = x when the question asks for x as the subject.

commonErrors.misconception: Trying to find a numerical value for x when none exists.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Trying to find a numerical value for x when none exists.

examTip.value: Ask yourself what has been done to the wanted letter, then do the opposite to both sides. That single question drives every change-of-subject question in the syllabus.
